entities.summary: Kiyoshi Ogawa was a Japanese naval aviator ensign (少尉) of the Imperial Japanese Navy during World War II. As a kamikaze pilot, Ensign Ogawa's final action took place on May 11, 1945, during the Battle of Okinawa. Piloting a bomb-laden Mitsubishi Zero fighter during Operation Kikusui No. 6, Ogawa flew through American anti-aircraft fire and struck the aircraft carrier USS Bunker Hill, less than one minute after his flight leader, sub-lieutenant Seizō Yasunori, crashed into the ship. Ogawa dropped a 250-kilogram (551 lb) bomb, never pulled out of the dive, and crashed deliberately into the flight deck near the control tower of the aircraft carrier.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kiyoshi Ogawa's kamikaze mission on May 11, 1945, resulted in the sinking of USS Bunker Hill, a significant loss for the United States during World War II. This action had regional consequences, contributing to Japan's continued resistance against Allied forces.
